The operation respects the user's account status (suspended accounts can still view their own profile) and returns current data reflecting any recent moderator actions or account changes.

Related operations: The PUT /my/profile endpoint allows users to update their own profile information such as email or username. Account creation and authentication are handled through separate authentication service endpoints (not managed by this API).

responseBody.description: The authenticated user's complete profile information including account details and verification state

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates the authenticated user's profile information in the discussion board system. Supports updates to user account details such as email address and username for both contributors and moderators. The operation validates that requested changes comply with business rules (email uniqueness, username uniqueness, format requirements) before persisting updates to either the discussion_board_contributors or discussion_board_moderators table. The operation records the update timestamp and returns the updated profile information confirming all changes. Moderators and contributors retain the ability to update account information while suspended, but updates are restricted if the account is deleted.
operations.summary: Update the authenticated user's profile information
operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's profile information such as email address and username.

This operation allows authenticated users (contributors and moderators) to modify their own account information. The operation accepts updates to fields such as email address and username while enforcing uniqueness constraints and format validation rules. Email must be in valid format (user@domain.com) and unique across all accounts of the same user type. Username must be 3-50 characters, alphanumeric with underscores, and unique across accounts of the same user type.

The operation updates the appropriate table (discussion_board_contributors or discussion_board_moderators) based on the authenticated user's type. The updated_at timestamp is automatically recorded to reflect the modification time. All updates are applied atomically; if any validation fails, no changes are persisted.

Security considerations: This operation requires authentication via JWT token. Users can only update their own profile; cross-user profile modifications are not permitted. Certain fields such as account_status, password (managed through separate password change endpoint), and moderation_tier (for moderators) cannot be modified through this operation. Password changes are handled through a dedicated password management endpoint that requires additional verification. Account status changes can only be performed by moderators through administrative operations.

Validation rules: Email addresses must follow RFC 5321 standards. Usernames must match pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{3,50}$. Duplicate email or username values across the user's account type will result in HTTP 409 Conflict error with descriptive message indicating which field caused the conflict.

Related operations: GET /my/profile retrieves current profile information. Separate password change endpoint handles password updates with additional security requirements. Account status changes and other administrative modifications are performed by moderators through moderation endpoints.

requestBody.description: Updated profile information including email and username

responseBody.description: The updated user profile information confirming all changes were applied

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation allows an authenticated contributor to change their account password. It operates on the discussion_board_contributors table and requires the user to provide their current password for verification before allowing the password change. The new password must meet security requirements: minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Upon successful password change, all existing sessions for the contributor are invalidated for security purposes, forcing re-authentication on all devices.
operations.summary: Change contributor account password
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authenticated contributors to update their account password. The operation requires verification of the current password to prevent unauthorized password changes. The new password must meet security requirements with a minimum of 8 characters including uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.

The password_hash field in the discussion_board_contributors table stores the Bcrypt-hashed password with a minimum of 12 salt rounds. When a contributor changes their password, the password_changed_at timestamp is updated, and all active sessions are invalidated immediately for security purposes.

Security considerations include rate limiting on password change attempts and logging of password change events for audit trails. The operation is restricted to authenticated contributors who must provide their current password before the new password is accepted.

Related operations include account deletion (POST /profile/delete) and session management. A successful password change will require the contributor to log in again on all devices, as all existing session tokens are revoked.

requestBody.description: Current password and new password for the password change operation

responseBody.description: Confirmation message indicating successful password change

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: This operation allows an authenticated contributor to delete their own account. It operates on the discussion_board_contributors table and implements soft deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time. The contributor's account status is changed to 'deleted', marking the account for deletion while preserving all data for audit and recovery purposes. Soft-deleted accounts are retained for 6 months to enable recovery; after 6 months, the account and associated data can be permanently purged. The operation requires password verification to prevent accidental or unauthorized account deletion.
operations.summary: Soft-delete contributor account
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authenticated contributors to delete their own account through a soft-delete operation. The account is marked for deletion by setting the deleted_at timestamp to the current time and changing the account_status to 'deleted', while all data is retained in the database for audit trail and recovery purposes.

The discussion_board_contributors table uses soft deletion to preserve contributor information and maintain data integrity for associated articles and comments. Deleted accounts are retained for 6 months to enable recovery through administrator support; after 6 months, the account and related data can be permanently purged from the system.

Security and authorization require password verification before account deletion to prevent unauthorized or accidental deletion. The operation disables all active sessions for the contributor, preventing further access immediately after deletion.

Upon successful deletion, the contributor can no longer log in, create articles, post comments, or access any features. Articles and comments created by the deleted account remain visible in the system but are associated with a deleted contributor account. Related operations include password change (POST /profile/change-password) and account recovery (if implemented).

requestBody.description: Password verification for account deletion confirmation

responseBody.description: Confirmation message indicating successful account deletion

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific discussion board contributor by their unique identifier. It operates on the discussion_board_contributors table from the Prisma schema and returns comprehensive contributor account data including email, username, account status, and authentication metadata. The operation requires an authenticated request and appropriate authorization to access contributor information.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific discussion board contributor's detailed account information
operations.description:
Fetch complete information about a discussion board contributor account by their unique identifier. This operation returns all relevant contributor metadata including email address, username, account status, email verification state, creation and modification timestamps, and last login information.

The contributor entity represents registered user accounts capable of creating articles and posting comments on the discussion board. Each contributor maintains unique email and username fields enforced at the database level. Account status can be 'active' for normal operations, 'suspended' for temporary bans, 'restricted' for limited posting permissions, or 'deleted' for accounts marked for soft deletion.

Security and access control are important considerations. The operation validates the contributor ID exists and is accessible. Email addresses and authentication-related timestamps should be treated as sensitive information requiring appropriate authorization checks. This operation complements list retrieval operations (PATCH /articles) and other contributor-related endpoints.

The response includes timestamp information for account creation, last modification, last successful login, and password changes. The deleted_at field indicates soft deletion status; accounts are retained for 6 months after deletion to enable recovery before permanent purge. Email verification status determines whether the account can perform authenticated actions like posting articles or comments.

parameters.name: contributorId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target discussion board contributor

responseBody.description: Complete contributor account information including authentication status and profile details

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, filtered list of discussion board articles with advanced search, sorting, and filtering capabilities. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table from the Prisma schema and supports complex queries for discovering articles based on status, category, author, publication dates, and text search across title and content fields. The operation returns articles with summary information optimized for list display, including view counts, comment counts, and pinned status.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of discussion board articles
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated collection of discussion board articles with comprehensive search and filtering capabilities. This operation provides advanced discovery features for finding articles based on publication status, category assignment, author, creation/publication dates, pinned status, and full-text search across article titles and content.

The article entity represents core discussion content in the platform. Articles progress through a defined lifecycle: draft (author composition) → pending_approval (moderator review) → published (publicly visible) → archived or deleted (removed from active listings). Only published articles are publicly visible by default, though filtering options allow access to other statuses based on authorization levels.

The operation supports multiple filtering dimensions: status filtering (published, draft, pending_approval, rejected, archived, deleted), category filtering for topic organization, author filtering to find contributions by specific contributors, date range filtering for discovery by creation or publication time, and full-text search capabilities across title and content fields. Sorting options include creation date, publication date, view count, comment count, and pinned status.

Pagination is implemented with configurable page sizes and offsets to handle large article collections efficiently. The response includes summary-level information optimized for listing displays, including cached comment counts for performance, view counts for popularity metrics, pinned status for featured article highlighting, and locked status for editorial control. Related operations include detailed article retrieval (GET /articles/{articleId}) and article creation/modification endpoints.

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, pagination parameters, and sorting preferences for article discovery

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of article summaries matching search and filter criteria

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation creates a new article in the discussion board system, allowing authenticated contributors to submit economic and political discussion content. The operation accepts article title, content, category selection, and optional attachments. Upon creation, the article is initialized in 'draft' status, allowing the contributor to save their work and return later to continue editing. The operation operates on the discussion_board_articles table and associates the article with the authenticated contributor through the discussion_board_contributor_id foreign key. Articles must meet validation requirements: title 5-200 characters, content 50-50,000 characters, and category must be one of the predefined values from article_categories table. Attachments are optional (0-10 files) with file size limits enforced during upload.
operations.summary: Create a new article draft in the discussion board
operations.description:
Create a new discussion board article in draft status. This operation allows authenticated contributors to compose articles on economic and political topics before submitting them for moderator review.

The article is initialized with 'draft' status, allowing the contributor to save their work, close the browser, and return later to continue editing without requiring moderator approval at this stage. The system automatically records the contributor's ID as the article author and sets the creation timestamp. All article content and metadata are stored in the discussion_board_articles table with references to the author contributor and selected category.

Validation is enforced for all required fields: title must be 5-200 characters describing the article topic, content must be 50-50,000 characters containing the main discussion or analysis, and category must be selected from the predefined article categories (Economics, Politics, Policy, Trade, Markets, Regulation, International, Analysis, Opinion, Other Discussion). Invalid category selections are rejected with an error listing valid options.

The operation supports optional attachment uploads (images and documents) up to a maximum of 10 files per article. Attachments are validated for file type (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP for images; PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT, XLS, XLSX for documents) and size limits (10MB for images, 25MB for documents) during the creation request. Multiple attachments can be provided in a single request.

Security: Only authenticated contributors can access this endpoint. The operation requires valid JWT token authentication and the contributor's account must be in 'active' status with verified email address. The system automatically associates the created article with the authenticated user's contributor ID, preventing contributors from creating articles on behalf of others. The operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized if authentication is missing or invalid, and HTTP 403 Forbidden if the contributor account is not active or email is unverified.

Related operations: After creating an article in draft status, the contributor uses PUT /articles/{articleId} to edit the article content before submission. Once ready for moderation review, the contributor calls PATCH /articles/{articleId}/submit to transition from draft to pending_approval status. GET /articles/{articleId} retrieves the full article details including metadata and attachments.

requestBody.description: Article creation payload including title, content, category, optional description, and attachment uploads

responseBody.description: Created article object with full details including ID, author info, timestamps, and attachment metadata

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the complete details of a single article from the discussion board, identified by its unique article ID. The operation operates on the discussion_board_articles table and implements visibility controls based on article status and user role. Published articles are visible to all users (guests, contributors, and moderators), while draft, pending_approval, and rejected articles are only visible to their authors and moderators. The response includes article metadata (title, content, status, author, timestamps), complete attachment list with file metadata (original filename, file size, upload timestamp, display URL), and counts of views and comments. The operation enforces soft delete visibility - articles with deleted_at timestamp are not accessible to regular users.
operations.summary: Retrieve a complete article with all details and attachments
operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a specific article from the discussion board, including content, metadata, all attachments, and related information. This operation implements comprehensive visibility controls ensuring users can only access articles they have permission to view.

Published articles (status='published') are visible to all users: guests (unauthenticated), contributors, and moderators. Draft, pending_approval, and rejected articles are restricted to their original authors and moderators only. Attempting to access a non-published article without authorization returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with message 'You do not have permission to view this article.' Deleted articles (with deleted_at timestamp) are not accessible to regular users; only moderators can view deleted articles for audit trail purposes.

The response includes complete article information: title, content body, current status (draft/pending_approval/published/rejected/archived/deleted), author name and ID, creation and modification timestamps, published_at timestamp (null if not yet published), approval information (approver moderator ID and approval notes if approved), and rejection information (rejection reason if rejected). View count and comment count are included to help users identify popular discussions.

Attachment metadata is returned for all files associated with the article, including original filename, file type, file size in bytes, MIME type for proper browser rendering, upload timestamp, uploader contributor ID, and display URL for accessing the file. Attachments are ordered by upload sequence (first uploaded appears first in the list). For articles in draft status, only the author and moderators can view attachment information. For published articles, attachment information is visible to all users.

Moderation metadata is included for moderators viewing articles: is_pinned flag (whether article is featured), is_locked flag (whether new comments are blocked), last_edited_by contributor ID if article has been edited after creation. Moderators also see the complete audit trail of modifications and approval history.

Security: Public read access is available for published articles - no authentication required. Non-published articles require authentication and ownership or moderator privileges. The operation returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized if a non-published article is requested without authentication. HTTP 403 Forbidden is returned if the authenticated user is not the author and not a moderator. HTTP 404 Not Found is returned if the article ID does not exist or has been permanently deleted (not soft-deleted).

Performance: Article data including content and attachments are optimized for single-article retrieval with database queries leveraging indexes on article ID and foreign key relationships. Related operations: PATCH /articles searches and lists articles with filtering and pagination. PUT /articles/{articleId} edits article content if permitted. DELETE /articles/{articleId} removes articles if permitted. GET /articles/{articleId}/comments retrieves comments on the article.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the target article to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete article details including content, metadata, status, attachments, and moderator information

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Article must be created before it can be retrieved. The POST operation creates an article with a generated articleId that is needed for the GET operation to function.

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing discussion board article with new content, title, category, or status. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and allows authenticated contributors to modify their own articles. The operation validates that the article exists, belongs to the contributor, and applies appropriate authorization checks based on contributor role.
operations.summary: Update an article with revised content or metadata
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article by providing new content, title, category assignment, or status change. This operation allows contributors to revise their own articles in draft or rejected states.

Contributor-specific permissions apply: contributors can only modify their own unpublished articles. Article status transitions follow the defined workflow:
- Draft articles: Contributor can update content/title freely and transition to pending_approval
- Rejected articles: Contributor can update content and resubmit for approval

The operation automatically updates the modified timestamp (updated_at) and records the user who performed the edit (last_edited_by_contributor_id). The operation validates the article belongs to the authenticated contributor before allowing modifications.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching articles by status or category, POST /articles to create new articles, GET /articles/{articleId} to retrieve article details before updating, and DELETE endpoints for article removal.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the discussion board article to be updated. Must reference an existing article owned by the authenticated contributor.

requestBody.description: Article update data including content and title. Validation constraints: Title 5-200 characters, Content 50-50,000 characters.

responseBody.description: Complete updated discussion board article with all fields including status, metadata, and audit timestamps reflecting the modification.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing discussion board article's administrative metadata and status. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and permits moderators to update article status, approval notes, and moderation flags on any article. The operation validates that the article exists and applies moderator-level authorization checks.
operations.summary: Update article status and moderation metadata as moderator
operations.description:
Update an existing discussion board article's status, approval notes, pins, and locks as a moderator. This operation allows moderators to approve or reject articles, add approval feedback, pin articles for featured display, lock articles from further comments, or archive articles.

Moderator-specific permissions apply: only moderators can execute this operation and can update any article regardless of authorship. Article status transitions follow moderation workflow:
- Pending approval: Moderator can approve (→published) or reject (→rejected)
- Published articles: Moderator can update pins/locks and transition to archived
- Rejected articles: Moderator can delete
- Archived articles: Moderator can restore or delete

The operation automatically updates the modified timestamp (updated_at) and records the moderator user ID. When moderators approve articles, the published_at timestamp is set and the article becomes publicly visible. Moderators can add approval_notes (max 1,000 characters) or rejection_reason (max 500 characters) to provide feedback to contributors.

Related operations include PATCH /articles for searching articles by status or category, GET /articles/{articleId} to retrieve article details before moderating.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the discussion board article to be moderated. Must reference an existing article.

requestBody.description: Moderator update data including status transitions, approval/rejection notes, pin flags, and lock flags. Approval notes max 1,000 characters, Rejection reason max 500 characters.

responseBody.description: Complete updated discussion board article reflecting moderator actions including status, approval metadata, and administrative flags.

operations.name: updateByModerator

operations.specification: This operation removes a discussion board article from the system through soft deletion or permanent deletion. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and allows contributors to remove their own articles. The operation handles cascade deletion of associated comments and attachments when performing hard deletion, or marks the article as deleted using soft deletion for audit trail preservation.
operations.summary: Delete an article (contributor)
operations.description:
Remove a discussion board article from the system as a contributor by either soft deletion (preserving record for compliance) or permanent deletion (erase all data). Soft deletion sets the deleted_at timestamp, removing public visibility while maintaining audit trail and historical records for compliance purposes. Hard deletion completely removes the article record and associated data from the database.

Contributor-specific authorization applies: contributors can only delete their own articles. Articles in draft status can be deleted by contributors at any time. Published or archived articles can only be deleted by moderators (use moderator delete endpoint). The operation validates article ownership before processing.

Cascade behavior when article is deleted:
- All comments on the article are deleted (using same soft or hard delete strategy)
- All article attachment records are removed from storage
- View counts and statistics are cleared

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} to verify article existence, PATCH /articles to list articles (which excludes deleted articles in default view), and PUT /articles/{articleId} to update article status before deletion.

Articles cannot be recovered after hard deletion, so users should confirm deletion intent before executing this operation.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the discussion board article to be deleted by contributor. Must reference an existing article owned by the authenticated contributor.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of deleted article with final state including deletion timestamp.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation removes a discussion board article from the system through soft deletion or permanent deletion. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table and permits moderators to remove any article. The operation handles cascade deletion of associated comments and attachments when performing hard deletion, or marks the article as deleted using soft deletion for compliance and audit trail preservation.
operations.summary: Delete an article (moderator)
operations.description:
Remove a discussion board article from the system as a moderator using soft deletion (preserving record for compliance) or permanent deletion (erase all data). Only moderators can execute this operation. Moderators can delete any article regardless of authorship or status.

Soft deletion sets the deleted_at timestamp, removing public visibility while maintaining audit trail and historical records for compliance and regulatory purposes. Hard deletion completely removes the article record and associated data from the database.

Cascade behavior when article is deleted:
- All comments on the article are deleted (using same soft or hard delete strategy)
- All article attachment records are removed from storage
- Moderation history is preserved in audit trail for compliance
- View counts and statistics are cleared

Related operations include GET /articles/{articleId} to verify article state, PATCH /articles to list articles (which excludes deleted articles in default view).

Articles cannot be recovered after hard deletion. Moderators should document deletion rationale in system logs.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the discussion board article to be deleted by moderator. Must reference an existing article.

responseBody.description: Confirmation of deleted article with final state including deletion timestamp.

operations.name: eraseByModerator

operations.specification: This operation allows moderators to approve a pending article for publication. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, transitioning the article from pending_approval status to published status. The moderator can provide optional approval notes that are stored alongside the approval decision. The operation automatically records the moderator who performed the approval, sets the published_at timestamp, and creates an immutable audit trail entry in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for compliance tracking. Article identifiers are UUID format matching the primary key in discussion_board_articles. Only users with moderator permissions can execute this operation.
operations.summary: Approve a pending article for publication with optional moderator notes
operations.description:
Approve a discussion board article that is currently in pending_approval status, transitioning it to published status for public visibility. Moderators use this operation after reviewing article content for compliance with community guidelines. Optional approval notes (maximum 1,000 characters) can be included to provide feedback to the contributor about why the article was approved or suggestions for future contributions.

The operation updates the article's status to 'published', records the moderator performing the approval via the approved_by_moderator_id field, and sets the published_at timestamp to the current time. An immutable audit trail entry is automatically created in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table with action_type 'approved' and the approval notes, providing permanent compliance documentation.

Security context: Only authenticated moderators can invoke this operation. The moderator's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and recorded in the article's approved_by_moderator_id field. Articles must be in pending_approval status to be approved; attempting to approve articles in other statuses will result in validation errors.

Related operations: Before approving, moderators typically retrieve pending articles using the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles with status filter). The rejection endpoint (POST /articles/{articleId}/reject) is used if the moderator decides the article does not meet community standards.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to approve (UUID format)

requestBody.description: Moderator approval decision with optional feedback notes

responseBody.description: Updated article object with published status and approval metadata

operations.name: approve

operations.specification: This operation allows moderators to reject a pending article, preventing its publication and returning it to the author for revision. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, transitioning the article from pending_approval status to rejected status. The moderator must provide a rejection reason (required, maximum 500 characters) explaining why the article does not meet community standards. The operation automatically records the moderator who performed the rejection and creates an immutable audit trail entry in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for compliance tracking. Article identifiers are UUID format matching the primary key in discussion_board_articles. Only users with moderator permissions can execute this operation.
operations.summary: Reject a pending article with required moderator feedback
operations.description:
Reject a discussion board article that is currently in pending_approval status, transitioning it to rejected status and preventing publication. Moderators use this operation after reviewing article content and determining it does not meet community guidelines or quality standards. A rejection reason is required (maximum 500 characters) to explain to the contributor why the article was declined and provide guidance for revision and resubmission.

The operation updates the article's status to 'rejected', records the moderator performing the rejection, and stores the rejection_reason in the article record for contributor reference. An immutable audit trail entry is automatically created in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table with action_type 'rejected' and the rejection reason, providing permanent compliance documentation and accountability tracking.

Security context: Only authenticated moderators can invoke this operation. The moderator's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token. Articles must be in pending_approval status to be rejected; attempting to reject articles in other statuses will result in validation errors. The rejection reason provides critical feedback helping contributors understand how to revise their article for future resubmission.

Related operations: Before rejecting, moderators typically retrieve pending articles using the article search endpoint (PATCH /articles with status filter). The approval endpoint (POST /articles/{articleId}/approve) is used if the moderator determines the article meets community standards. After rejection, contributors can edit their article and resubmit for review.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to reject (UUID format)

requestBody.description: Moderator rejection decision with required feedback reason

responseBody.description: Updated article object with rejected status and rejection reason

operations.name: reject

operations.specification: This operation archives a published or pending article, removing it from active listings and search results while preserving the record for historical reference. Operating on the discussion_board_articles table, this action updates the article status to 'archived' and creates an audit trail entry in discussion_board_article_moderation_history. Only moderators can archive articles. Archived articles remain accessible to moderators but are hidden from contributor and public views, supporting content lifecycle management and compliance retention requirements.
operations.summary: Archive a discussion board article and remove it from active listings
operations.description:
Perform a moderation action to archive a discussion board article. This operation transitions an article from published or pending_approval status to archived status, effectively removing it from user-facing listings and search results while maintaining the complete record in the system for audit and compliance purposes.

Archiving is a reversible moderation action that moderators use to manage content visibility without permanent deletion. Archived articles are no longer discoverable through normal browsing and search, but remain queryable by moderators for historical review and audit trail purposes. The article's view count and comment history are preserved.

This operation requires moderator-level permissions and creates an immutable audit trail entry recording the archival action, timestamp, and moderating user. The archival action is tracked in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table for complete accountability and compliance documentation of all moderator decisions affecting articles.

Only articles with status 'published' or 'pending_approval' can be archived. Articles already in 'archived', 'rejected', 'draft', or 'deleted' status cannot be archived. The operation returns the complete updated article record reflecting the new archived status and updated_at timestamp.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the article to archive

requestBody.description: Archival action details including moderator's removal reason for compliance documentation

responseBody.description: Complete article record with updated status set to 'archived' and current moderation state

operations.name: archive

prerequisites.description: Article must be created before it can be archived. The archive operation requires a valid articleId referencing an existing article with status either 'published' or 'pending_approval'.

operations.specification: This operation pins an article to the top of listings for featured display, highlighting important or valuable discussion content. Operating on the discussion_board_articles table, this action sets the is_pinned flag to true and creates an audit trail entry in discussion_board_article_moderation_history. Only moderators can pin articles. Pinned articles appear before all unpinned articles in browsing and search views, increasing visibility and reader engagement with moderator-selected content.
operations.summary: Pin a discussion board article to featured display at top of listings
operations.description:
Perform a moderation action to pin a discussion board article to the top of content listings for featured visibility. This operation marks the article as pinned, causing it to appear above all unpinned articles in category browsing, search results, and article listings throughout the discussion board interface.

Pinning is a curation tool that moderators use to highlight high-quality discussions, important announcements, or particularly valuable contributor insights. Pinned articles maintain their original publication date and sorting but are sorted to the top of result sets to ensure maximum visibility. Multiple articles can be pinned simultaneously, with their relative order determined by secondary sort criteria.

This operation requires moderator-level permissions and creates an immutable audit trail entry recording the pinning action, timestamp, and moderating user in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table. The pinning action is reversible through the unpin operation, allowing moderators to adjust featured content as discussions evolve and new topics emerge.

Only articles with status 'published' can be pinned. Articles with status 'draft', 'pending_approval', 'rejected', 'archived', or 'deleted' cannot be pinned. The operation returns the complete updated article record reflecting the pinned status and updated_at timestamp.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the article to pin

responseBody.description: Complete article record with updated is_pinned flag set to true and current state

operations.name: pin

prerequisites.description: Article must be created before it can be pinned. The pin operation requires a valid articleId referencing an existing article with status 'published'.

operations.specification: This operation unpins a featured article from the top of discussion board listings. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_pinned boolean field. Only moderators can perform this action. The operation represents a moderator decision to remove an article from featured display, making it appear in normal chronological order with other articles. This action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as an audit trail entry.
operations.summary: Unpin a featured article from discussion board listings
operations.description:
Remove a pinned article from featured display at the top of article listings. This moderator action returns the article to normal chronological sorting with other articles.

Pinned articles are featured prominently in all browsing and search views. Unpinning removes this special status. The article remains published and visible in normal listings, but will no longer appear at the top. This operation is available only to authenticated moderators with full moderation permissions.

The unpinning action is recorded in the moderation history audit trail with the moderator's ID, timestamp, and action type (unpinned). The article's is_pinned field is updated to false. Related operations include locking articles (POST /articles/{articleId}/lock) and archiving articles for complete removal from listings.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to unpin

responseBody.description: The unpinned article with updated pin status

operations.name: unpin

prerequisites.description: An article must be created before it can be unpinned. This operation creates the article resource that the unpin operation will modify.

operations.specification: This operation locks an article preventing further comments while keeping the article visible with existing comments. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_locked boolean field. Only moderators can perform this action. Locking prevents new comments from being posted on the article while maintaining visibility of existing discussion. This action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as an audit trail entry.
operations.summary: Lock an article to prevent new comments
operations.description:
Lock an article to prevent new comments while keeping the article and existing comments visible to users. This moderator action is used to end discussion on sensitive or resolved topics while preserving the historical record.

Locked articles remain fully visible in listings and search results with all existing comments intact. Users cannot post new comments on locked articles, but can still view the existing discussion. The is_locked field is updated to true. This operation is available only to authenticated moderators with full moderation permissions.

The locking action is recorded in the moderation history audit trail with the moderator's ID, timestamp, and action type (locked). This creates an immutable record for compliance and accountability purposes. Related operations include pinning articles for featured display (POST /articles/{articleId}/pin) and archiving articles for complete removal from public listings.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to lock

responseBody.description: The locked article with updated lock status

operations.name: lock

prerequisites.description: An article must be created before it can be locked. This operation creates the article resource that the lock operation will modify.

operations.specification: This operation unlocks a discussion board article, enabling contributors to post new comments on the article again. It operates on the discussion_board_articles table, specifically modifying the is_locked boolean field. Only moderators with appropriate permissions can perform this action. The article must exist and be in a locked state. Upon successful unlock, the article becomes available for new comment submissions while preserving all existing comments and article content. This is a moderator-controlled action that reverses a prior lock operation, typically performed when moderation of discussions has concluded or when a lock was applied in error.
operations.summary: Unlock a discussion board article to allow new comments
operations.description:
Unlock a discussion board article, enabling contributors to post new comments on it again.

This operation allows moderators to remove comment restrictions from articles that were previously locked. Locked articles remain visible with all existing comments intact, but new comments cannot be posted. Unlocking restores the article to an open state where contributors can resume discussions.

The operation directly modifies the is_locked field in the discussion_board_articles table, setting it from true to false. This is a straightforward state transition that does not affect the article's content, publication status, or existing comments. The article must be in a published state and currently locked for this operation to succeed.

Moderator authentication is required for this privileged operation. The action is recorded in the discussion_board_article_moderation_history table as a moderation decision for audit and compliance purposes. This enables complete tracking of all moderation actions taken on articles throughout their lifecycle.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to unlock

responseBody.description: The unlocked article with all metadata and current state

operations.name: unlock

prerequisites.description: Article must exist before it can be unlocked. The POST /discussionBoard/contributor/articles operation creates a new article and returns its ID, which is required for the unlock operation to reference the correct article.

operations.specification: This operation uploads and attaches a file to a discussion board article. It operates on the discussion_board_article_attachments table, creating a new attachment record linked to the parent article. Contributors can attach images (jpg, png, gif, webp) and documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) to accompany their articles, with strict file size limits enforced (5MB for images, 25MB for documents). The operation stores file metadata including original filename, file type, MIME type, file size, and a display URL for accessing the attachment in the web interface. Multiple attachments per article are supported up to a maximum of 10 files. Attachments are managed through article operations and are automatically removed when the parent article is deleted.
operations.summary: Upload and attach a file to a discussion board article
operations.description:
Upload and attach a file to a discussion board article for supporting evidence, visual content, or supplementary documents.

This operation allows contributors to attach files to their articles during creation or editing. Supported file types include images (jpg, png, gif, webp) and documents (pdf, docx, xlsx, txt) with appropriate file size restrictions. Images are limited to 5MB while documents can be up to 25MB. Each article can have up to 10 attachments, providing flexibility for comprehensive documentation while preventing excessive file storage.

The operation validates the uploaded file against type and size constraints before storing the attachment metadata. The uploaded file is persisted to storage, and a display URL is generated for accessing the file through the web interface. File metadata is recorded including the original filename as provided by the uploader, the determined file type/extension, MIME type for proper browser handling, and the exact file size in bytes.

Attachment ownership is tracked through the uploaded_by_contributor_id field, recording which contributor uploaded each file. This enables audit trails and contributor-specific attachment management. Attachments are immutably linked to their parent article and cannot be reassigned or moved to different articles.

When an article transitions to published status, all existing attachments remain accessible and visible. When an article is deleted (either hard or soft delete), all associated attachments are automatically removed from both the database and storage to maintain data integrity and prevent orphaned files.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article to which the file will be attached

requestBody.description: File upload data including the file content and metadata

responseBody.description: The created attachment record with file metadata and access information

operations.name: attach

prerequisites.description: Article must exist before attachments can be added to it. The POST /discussionBoard/contributor/articles operation creates a new article and returns its ID, which is required to reference the parent article for attachment operations.

operations.specification: This operation removes a file attachment from a discussion board article. The attachment deletion API operates on the discussion_board_article_attachments table, removing the attachment metadata record and triggering deletion of the associated file from storage. Only the contributor who uploaded the attachment, the article author, or moderators with appropriate permissions can delete attachments. Hard deletion is applied - attachments are permanently removed from the system.
operations.summary: Remove a file attachment from a discussion board article
operations.description:
Delete a specific file attachment that was previously uploaded to accompany an article. This operation removes the attachment metadata record from the discussion_board_article_attachments table and triggers deletion of the physical file from storage.

The attachment must exist and be associated with the specified article. The operation validates that the requesting user has appropriate permissions to delete attachments - the contributor who uploaded the file, the article author, or a moderator with elevated privileges can perform this action.

Once deleted, the attachment cannot be recovered as permanent deletion is applied. The article itself remains unaffected by attachment deletion. If the article contains multiple attachments, only the specified attachment is removed.

This operation is commonly performed when: contributors remove accidentally uploaded files, moderators enforce content policies by removing inappropriate attachments, or users clean up outdated supporting materials. The operation supports audit logging to track which user deleted the attachment and when the deletion occurred.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article containing the attachment to be deleted

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the attachment file record to be deleted from the article

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated, searchable collection of comments posted on a specific discussion board article. The comments search API operates on the discussion_board_comments table, filtering by the specified article ID and supporting complex query criteria including comment content search, author filtering, date ranges, and sorting options. Supports nested comment threads by optionally returning parent comment references for context. Handles soft-deleted comments appropriately based on user permissions and authorization level.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of comments on a discussion board article
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of comments posted on a specific article, enabling users to browse discussions and moderate content. This operation queries the discussion_board_comments table filtered by the specified article ID, supporting comprehensive search and filtering capabilities.

The operation supports multiple search and filtering features including: full-text search within comment content, filtering by comment author (contributor), date range filtering to find recent or historical comments, sorting by creation date or reply count, and hierarchical thread support for nested replies. Users can retrieve top-level comments on the article or include nested replies based on parent comment relationships stored in the parent_comment_id field.

Permissions and visibility are context-aware: unauthenticated users see only published comments from non-archived articles, authenticated contributors see their own comments and published comments, and moderators see all comments including soft-deleted ones for content policy enforcement and audit trail maintenance. The response includes comprehensive comment metadata such as creation and modification timestamps, author contributor information, cached reply counts, and edit history.

Comments that have been soft-deleted (marked with is_deleted=true or deleted_at timestamp not null) are excluded from normal user views but remain visible to moderators for content moderation purposes and compliance auditing. The operation efficiently handles large comment threads through pagination and can display comment nesting information to preserve thread context.

Related operations: Create comment (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments), Update comment (PUT /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}), Delete comment (DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}), Get comment details (GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}).

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article whose comments are being retrieved

requestBody.description: Search criteria, filtering options, pagination parameters, and sorting preferences for comment retrieval

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of comment records matching the search criteria with author and thread information

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Article must be created and exist in the system before its comments can be retrieved. The article ID is required to filter and retrieve associated comments.

operations.specification: Create a new comment on a published discussion board article. This operation allows authenticated contributors to post comments to existing articles, enabling community discussion and engagement. The comment is published immediately without requiring moderator approval, though moderators retain the ability to edit or remove inappropriate comments. Comments support optional file attachments (images only) and can be nested replies to other comments or top-level comments on the article. The operation validates that the article exists and is published, creates the new comment with timestamps and contributor attribution, optionally processes attached images, and updates comment counts.
operations.summary: Create a new comment on a discussion board article
operations.description:
Create a new comment on a published discussion board article, enabling contributors to participate in discussions. This operation accepts comment content and optional image attachments, validates the article exists and is published, and immediately publishes the comment without moderator approval.

Comments support hierarchical threading where contributors can reply directly to articles or reply to specific comments. When replying to a comment, the parentCommentId field establishes the relationship and enables proper thread organization. Top-level comments have no parent and appear at the article level.

Each comment maintains creation and modification timestamps, contributor attribution, and soft deletion support. The operation automatically initializes the edit count to zero and reply count to zero for new comments. Comments include cached publication status of the parent article at creation time for audit purposes.

Optional image attachments (JPG, PNG, GIF formats) can be included with each comment, limited to 2 files per comment with 5MB size limits. The system validates attachment MIME types and stores metadata including original filenames and file sizes for proper display and storage management.

The operation requires authentication to identify the commenting contributor. Security considerations include rate limiting for comment creation, validation of article publication status, and protection against concurrent modification of parent articles or comments.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target article being commented on

requestBody.description: Comment content and optional attachment data for creating a new comment

responseBody.description: Newly created comment with all metadata and timestamps

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Article must be created and exist in published status before contributors can post comments on it. The operation validates that the target article is published before creating the comment.

operations.specification: Retrieve a specific comment by ID from a discussion board article. This operation fetches detailed comment information including the complete comment text, author details, creation and modification timestamps, edit history count, reply count, and nested comment structure for replies. The operation validates that both the article and comment exist, returns full comment details including author information and attachment metadata, and supports access control based on comment visibility and user authorization.
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific comment from a discussion board article
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific comment on a discussion board article. This operation returns the complete comment record including the comment text, author information, creation and modification timestamps, edit history, reply information, and associated image attachments.

The operation validates that the specified article exists and that the comment belongs to that article. Comments that have been soft-deleted may be returned based on authorization context, with the deletion status indicated in the response. The response includes metadata such as edit count (number of times the comment has been modified), reply count (number of direct replies to this comment), and cached article publication status at the time the comment was posted.

For threaded comments (replies to other comments), the response includes the parent comment reference enabling proper navigation of discussion threads. Comment attachments are included with metadata such as original filenames, file types, file sizes, and display URLs for accessing the attachment images.

Security and access control are implemented at the application layer. Public comments on published articles are generally visible to unauthenticated users. Comments on archived or deleted articles may have restricted visibility. Moderators can view all comments including deleted ones for review and audit purposes.

The operation supports retrieving recent comment modifications to track discussion activity and contributor participation. Related operations include listing all comments on an article (PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments for searching/filtering) and creating replies to this comment (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments with parentCommentId).

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article containing the target comment

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific comment to retrieve

responseBody.description: Complete comment details including content, metadata, author information, and attachments

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing comment on a published article within the discussion board system. The operation operates on the discussion_board_comments Prisma table, allowing contributors to modify their own comments or moderators to edit any comment for compliance. The endpoint requires the articleId and commentId path parameters to identify the target comment, and the request body contains the updated comment content. The operation validates that the comment exists, the user has appropriate permissions (author or moderator), and the updated content meets validation requirements (1-5000 characters). Upon successful update, the operation records the modification timestamp and increment the edit_count field.
operations.summary: Update an existing comment on a discussion board article
operations.description:
This operation allows a contributor to update their own comment or a moderator to edit any comment for compliance purposes. When a contributor submits a PUT request with updated comment content, the system validates ownership and enforces the 24-hour editing window for standard contributors. Moderators retain unlimited editing authority and can modify any comment on the platform.

The comment content is updated with the new text provided in the request body. The system validates that the updated content length is between 1 and 5,000 characters. If validation fails, the operation returns a 400 Bad Request error with specific validation details. The operation updates the comment's updated_at timestamp to reflect the modification time and increments the edit_count field to track revisions.

When a contributor edits their own comment within the allowed timeframe, the system marks the comment with an 'edited' indicator showing the last edited timestamp. When a moderator edits a comment, the system marks it with a '[edited by moderation]' indicator to maintain transparency. All edits are recorded in the moderation audit log with timestamps and editor information.

The operation checks article publication status to ensure comments can only be edited when the parent article is in an appropriate state. If a contributor attempts to edit a comment on a deleted or archived article, the operation returns HTTP 403 Forbidden. Moderators retain full editing capability regardless of article status. Upon successful update, the operation returns the updated comment object with current metadata including edit count and last modification timestamp.

parameters.name: articleId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article containing the comment being updated

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the comment to be updated

requestBody.description: Updated comment content and metadata for the modification

responseBody.description: Updated comment object with current content, edit count, and modification timestamp

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation removes a comment from a published article in the discussion board system. The operation works with the discussion_board_comments Prisma table, implementing soft deletion where the comment is marked as deleted (is_deleted=true, deleted_at timestamp recorded) but retained in the database for audit and compliance purposes. Contributors can delete their own comments at any time, while moderators can delete any comment with deletion reason tracking. The endpoint requires articleId and commentId path parameters to identify the target comment. Upon successful deletion, the comment no longer appears in discussion threads and is replaced with a deletion placeholder.
operations.summary: Delete a comment from a discussion board article using soft deletion
operations.description:
This operation removes a comment from public view by marking it as deleted, implementing soft deletion to preserve the audit trail and discussion thread coherence. When a contributor deletes their own comment, the system marks is_deleted=true and records the deletion timestamp in deleted_at. The deleted comment no longer appears in the discussion thread but is retained in the database for compliance and recovery purposes.

When a moderator deletes a comment, the system performs the same soft deletion but additionally records the moderation action in the audit log with the moderator ID, deletion timestamp, and optional reason for removal. The moderation log entry documents which content policy violation or community standard issue triggered the deletion, creating accountability for moderation actions.

If a comment has replies (nested comments), those replies remain in the database but their parent reference is updated to indicate the parent comment is no longer available. The discussion thread displays a placeholder message such as '[Parent comment was deleted]' to maintain conversation context.

The operation validates that the user has appropriate authority to delete the comment. Contributors can only delete their own comments, while moderators can delete any comment regardless of authorship. If a contributor attempts to delete another contributor's comment, the operation returns HTTP 403 Forbidden. If the comment has already been deleted, the operation idempotently succeeds (returns 200 OK) rather than returning a 404 error, as the desired state is already achieved.

The operation enforces business rules based on article state. If the article is archived or locked, contributors cannot delete comments (operation returns HTTP 403), though moderators retain full deletion capability. Upon successful deletion, the operation returns a success response confirming the comment has been marked for deletion with the deletion timestamp and affected reply count.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the article containing the comment to be deleted

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the comment to be deleted

responseBody.description: Confirmation of successful comment deletion with deletion timestamp and affected reply information

operations.specification: This operation creates a new image file attachment for a specific comment on a discussion board article. It operates on the discussion_board_comment_attachments table to store attachment metadata including file information, uploader identification, and storage location. The attachment is linked to a parent comment through the discussion_board_comment_id foreign key and tracks the uploading contributor through discussion_board_contributor_id. The operation validates file type (images only: JPG, PNG, GIF), enforces file size limits (maximum 5MB per attachment), and limits comments to 2 attachments maximum. Upon successful creation, the attachment record is persisted with generated UUID, original filename, MIME type, file size, upload timestamp, and display URL for retrieval.
operations.summary: Create a new image attachment for a discussion board comment
operations.description:
Create a new image file attachment for a specific comment within an article discussion. This operation enables contributors to attach supporting visual content (images only) to their comments to provide evidence, context, or visual references for their discussion contributions.

The attachment system enforces strict validation rules to maintain system integrity and performance. File uploads are limited to image formats (JPG, PNG, GIF) with a maximum size of 5MB per file. Each comment can have up to 2 image attachments to prevent excessive media bloat while allowing meaningful visual context. The system validates file type against MIME type to prevent format spoofing and ensures uploaded files conform to the allowed image specifications.

The attachment is immediately associated with the specified comment and contributor upon successful upload. The system generates a unique UUID identifier for the attachment, stores metadata including original filename for user display, file type for validation tracking, file size for storage accounting, and upload timestamp for audit purposes. A display URL is generated for accessing or embedding the attachment in the web interface.

Security and authorization considerations include contributor authentication - only authenticated contributors can upload attachments to their own comments. The system records the uploading contributor's ID for accountability and to enable future moderation features such as tracking attachment sources or removing attachments by specific users. File storage is handled separately with secure access controls to prevent unauthorized direct file access.

This operation should be used after successfully creating a comment (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments) when the contributor wants to attach supporting images. The attachment is immediately visible in the comment thread for other users to view. Related operations include retrieving comment details (GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}) to see all attachments, and deleting unwanted attachments (DELETE /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/attachments/{attachmentId}).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the discussion board article containing the target comment

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific comment to attach the image file to

requestBody.description: Image file attachment data including file content, metadata, and original filename

responseBody.description: Complete attachment record with generated UUID, file metadata, and display URL for access

operations.specification: This operation permanently removes a file attachment from a comment on a discussion board article. It operates on the discussion_board_comment_attachments table to delete attachment records identified by unique UUID. The operation locates the specific attachment by commentId and attachmentId, verifies the attachment exists and belongs to the specified comment, and removes the attachment record from the database. Upon successful deletion, the attachment is no longer accessible and the metadata record is removed. The parent comment's attachment list is updated to reflect the removal.
operations.summary: Delete an image attachment from a discussion board comment
operations.description:
Remove an image file attachment from a specific comment within an article discussion. This operation enables contributors to manage their own attachments by removing unwanted or erroneous files they have uploaded to their comments. Moderators can also remove inappropriate or policy-violating attachments when performing content moderation duties.

The operation locates the attachment by its unique identifier within the context of the specified comment and article. It verifies the attachment exists and belongs to the specified comment before proceeding with deletion. Upon confirmation, the attachment record is permanently removed from the database and the file is no longer accessible through the system. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes the attachment metadata and associated file.

Authorization and ownership validation ensure that only authorized parties can delete attachments. Contributors can delete attachments they have personally uploaded to their own comments. Moderators with elevated privileges can delete any attachment as part of their content moderation responsibilities. Attempting to delete an attachment not uploaded by the requesting contributor (unless moderator) will result in an authorization error.

After successful deletion, the comment's attachment list is immediately updated. If the deleted attachment was the last visual evidence supporting the comment's context, other users should be aware that the visual reference is no longer available. The operation does not modify the comment text itself - only the attachment association is removed.

This operation should be used when a contributor wants to remove an attachment they uploaded (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/attachments) or when a moderator needs to remove policy-violating content. Related operations include creating new attachments (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/attachments) and retrieving comment details including all remaining attachments (GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific comment containing the attachment to delete

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific attachment file to permanently remove

Upon confirmation, the attachment record is permanently removed from the database and the file is no longer accessible through the system. This is a hard delete operation that completely removes the attachment metadata and associated file.

Authorization and ownership validation ensure that only authorized parties can delete attachments. Contributors can delete attachments they have personally uploaded to their own comments. Attempting to delete an attachment uploaded by another contributor will result in an authorization error. Moderators with elevated privileges can delete any attachment as part of their content moderation responsibilities without ownership restrictions.

After successful deletion, the comment's attachment list is immediately updated. If the deleted attachment was the last visual evidence supporting the comment's context, other users should be aware that the visual reference is no longer available. The operation does not modify the comment text itself - only the attachment association is removed.

This operation should be used when a contributor wants to remove an attachment they uploaded (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/attachments) or when a moderator needs to remove policy-violating content. Related operations include creating new attachments (POST /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}/attachments) and retrieving comment details including all remaining attachments (GET /articles/{articleId}/comments/{commentId}).

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a comprehensive paginated list of all active article categories from the article_categories table. It enables users to browse available discussion topics and understand the organizational structure of the content ecosystem. The operation supports filtering, sorting, and pagination to handle category discovery in an efficient manner. Categories are ordered by their display_order field to maintain consistent UI presentation across the platform. Only active categories (is_active = true) are included in the response unless explicitly requested otherwise.
operations.summary: Retrieve a list of all discussion board article categories
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all active article categories from the discussion board. Categories provide the organizational structure for articles, enabling users to browse content by topic area including economics, politics, and other discussion areas.

This operation returns category metadata including the category code (machine-readable identifier), display name, description explaining the category scope, display order for UI rendering, and article count showing the number of published articles in each category. The category code uses lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance') and is between 5-50 characters. The display name is a human-readable title between 10-100 characters designed for user interface display in category selection dropdowns and article filters.

Categories are filtered to show only active categories (is_active = true), preventing users from selecting deprecated or inactive categories when creating articles. Soft-deleted categories are excluded from this list but may be referenced by historical articles for data integrity. The response includes a denormalized article_count field for each category, reflecting the number of published articles currently assigned to that category.

Results are ordered by the display_order field to ensure consistent presentation in user interfaces. Categories with lower display_order numbers appear first in the category menu, enabling administrators to control category prominence and browsing experience. This operation is typically called during article creation to populate category selection dropdowns or during initial page load to display the category navigation structure.

Related operations: Use GET /categories/{categoryId} to retrieve detailed information about a specific category.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of active article categories with metadata for display and selection

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information for a specific article category by its unique identifier (categoryId) from the article_categories table. The categoryId parameter uses UUID format to uniquely identify the category record. The operation returns comprehensive category metadata including all fields: code, name, description, display_order, is_active status, article_count, and audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at). This supports detailed category view displays, category-specific filtering in article search operations, and administrative category management interfaces.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific discussion board article category
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details for a specific article category identified by its unique UUID identifier. This operation returns the full category record including code, display name, description, activity status, and article statistics.

The category code is a unique machine-readable identifier (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance') consisting of 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens. The code serves as an alternative lookup key for API operations and internal system references. The category name is the human-readable display label between 10-100 characters used throughout the user interface for category selection and navigation.

The description field (up to 500 characters) provides detailed explanation of the category scope and purpose, helping users understand which articles should belong to that category. For example, the Economic Policy category description might explain: 'Articles about taxation, trade, regulation, and economic policy decisions'. The is_active status indicates whether this category is currently available for article submission - active categories appear in dropdown menus when users create articles, while inactive categories are hidden from new submissions but referenced by historical articles.

The article_count field contains a denormalized count of published articles currently assigned to this category. This count is maintained for display efficiency and reflects the number of articles users will find when browsing this category. The response also includes audit timestamps: created_at (when the category was initially created) and updated_at (when it was last modified), providing complete traceability of category lifecycle.

Soft-deleted categories (deleted_at is not null) should be excluded from this endpoint unless explicitly requested by authorized administrators. If a category has been deleted, the operation should either return a 404 Not Found response or return a restricted view of the data based on authorization level.

It operates on the content_guidelines table from the Prisma schema and supports filtering, sorting, and pagination to enable moderators and contributors to understand platform policies. The guidelines include policy codes, titles, detailed descriptions, severity levels, and applicability to articles/comments.
