Test successful moderator authentication with valid email and password credentials. Moderator provides registered email address and correct password along with session context (href and referrer URLs). The operation validates the email exists in the moderators table, verifies the bcrypt-hashed password matches, confirms email verification status is true, and checks account status is active. Upon successful validation, the system updates the last_login_at timestamp and returns JWT access and refresh tokens with proper expiration times. Verify the response includes moderator ID, email, username, verification status, account status (active), moderation tier (full), timestamps, and valid JWT tokens with access token expiration and refresh token expiration dates.

Test authentication rejection when moderator email has not been verified. Moderator provides valid credentials (registered email and correct password matching bcrypt hash) along with session context (href and referrer), but the email_verified field in the database is false. The operation validates the email and password successfully but rejects the login attempt because email verification is incomplete. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error response and does not issue JWT tokens. This validates the business rule that moderators cannot access moderation tools until completing email verification.

Test authentication rejection for deleted moderator accounts. Moderator provides valid credentials (registered email and correct password) along with session context (href and referrer), but the account_status field is 'deleted'. The operation validates the email and password but rejects the login attempt because the account has been marked for deletion. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error and does not issue JWT tokens, protecting deleted accounts from unauthorized access.

Test authentication rejection with incorrect password. Moderator provides a registered email address that exists in the database, but supplies an incorrect password that does not match the bcrypt-hashed password_hash. The operation validates that the email exists but password verification fails against the stored hash. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error without revealing whether the email exists in the database (security best practice to prevent email enumeration attacks). The operation should not issue JWT tokens.

Test password complexity validation during authentication. Moderator provides a valid registered email with a password that appears valid but fails complexity requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character). The operation validates password complexity against stored requirements and rejects authentication if the password does not meet complexity standards. Verify the system returns an appropriate error indicating password complexity failure.

Test that session context (href and referrer URLs) is properly captured during authentication. Moderator provides valid credentials along with the current page URL (href) and previous page URL (referrer) for session audit trail and security tracking. The operation accepts both mandatory session context fields (href and referrer are required per schema) along with optional client IP address. Verify the authenticated response is returned and can be used for subsequent authenticated requests. The session context should be recorded for audit trail purposes.

Test complete response structure validation for successful moderator authentication. Verify the response includes all required fields: moderator ID (UUID format), email address, username (3-50 characters, alphanumeric and underscore only), email_verified boolean status, account_status enum (active/suspended/deleted), moderation_tier constant (full), created_at timestamp, updated_at timestamp, optional deleted_at timestamp (null for active accounts), optional last_login_at timestamp. Verify the token object contains access token (JWT string), refresh token (JWT string), expired_at ISO 8601 timestamp, and refreshable_until ISO 8601 timestamp. Confirm last_login_at timestamp is updated to current time upon successful authentication.

Test successful JWT access token refresh using a valid refresh token. Moderator provides a valid refresh token previously issued during login or registration. The operation validates that the refresh token is valid (not malformed), has not expired, and belongs to an existing moderator account in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. The operation checks that the associated moderator's account_status is 'active' and email_verified is true. Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued with a new expiration time, allowing continued authenticated access to moderation features. Verify the response returns moderator information and new token object with both access and refresh tokens along with updated expiration timestamps.

Test token refresh rejection with an invalid refresh token. Moderator provides a refresh token that is malformed, expired, or does not exist in the discussion_board_moderator_sessions table. The operation validates the token against the session store and fails to find a valid session entry. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error and does not issue new tokens. This prevents access using invalid or expired refresh tokens.

Test token refresh rejection when the refresh token has expired. Moderator provides a refresh token that was valid but has passed its refreshable_until expiration timestamp. The operation validates the token expiration against the current time and finds the token has expired. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error indicating token expiration and does not issue new tokens. The moderator must re-authenticate with credentials to obtain new tokens.

Test token refresh rejection when the moderator account has been suspended after token issuance. Moderator provides a valid and unexpired refresh token, but the associated moderator's account_status has been changed to 'suspended' since token issuance. The operation validates the token structure and session entry but checks the current account status and finds it is not 'active'. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error preventing token refresh for suspended accounts, effectively terminating their authenticated sessions.

Test token refresh rejection when the moderator account has been deleted after token issuance. Moderator provides a valid and unexpired refresh token, but the associated moderator's account_status has been changed to 'deleted'. The operation validates the token and checks the current account status, finding it is marked for deletion. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error and does not issue new tokens, preventing access by deleted accounts.

Test token refresh rejection when moderator email has been unverified after token issuance. Moderator provides a valid and unexpired refresh token, but the associated moderator's email_verified field has been set to false. The operation validates the token structure and session but checks the current email verification status and finds it is false. Verify the system returns an appropriate authentication error preventing token refresh for unverified accounts, enforcing the business rule that moderators must have verified email addresses.

Test complete response structure validation for successful token refresh. Verify the response includes all moderator information fields: ID (UUID), email, username, email_verified status, account_status enum, moderation_tier (full), created_at, updated_at, deleted_at (optional), last_login_at (optional). Verify the token object contains new access token and refresh token (JWTs), expired_at ISO 8601 timestamp for access token, and refreshable_until ISO 8601 timestamp for refresh token. Confirm the new access token has a later expiration time than the original and can be used for subsequent authenticated requests.

Test that token refresh maintains moderator session continuity without re-authentication. Moderator successfully obtains initial access and refresh tokens during login. Without re-entering credentials, moderator uses the refresh token to obtain a new access token before the original expires. Verify the new access token can be used for authenticated moderation operations, effectively extending the session lifetime. This validates the intended use case of refresh tokens for maintaining continuous authenticated access without requiring credential re-entry.

Test successful password reset request initiation with a valid registered contributor email. The system should validate the email format, verify it exists in the contributor database, generate a secure time-limited reset token (valid for 30 minutes), and send it to the registered email address. Validate that the operation returns success regardless of whether the email is actually registered (to prevent account enumeration attacks). Verify that the generated token is cryptographically secure and cannot be predicted.

Test password reset request with an email address not registered in the system. The operation should return a generic success response without revealing whether the email exists or if the account is active/suspended/deleted. This prevents attackers from enumerating valid email addresses in the system. Verify that no token is actually generated or sent for non-existent accounts, but the API response appears identical to successful requests.

Test password reset request with invalid email formats such as missing @ symbol, missing domain, invalid characters, or malformed addresses. The system should reject these requests with validation errors indicating the email format requirement. Verify that proper email validation is applied before any database queries are performed.

Test password reset request with empty or null email field. The system should reject this as a required field validation error. Verify that the API properly handles missing required parameters and returns appropriate validation error responses.

Test that password reset requests handle email addresses case-insensitively (e.g., User@Example.com should match user@example.com). Email addresses are case-insensitive by RFC standards. Verify that the system normalizes email addresses for comparison and token generation, and that the token can be used regardless of email case variations in the reset-password request.

Test that repeated password reset requests from the same email address within a short time period properly implement rate limiting. Each new request should invalidate the previous token, keeping only the most recent token valid. Verify that the system tracks request timestamps and enforces rate limits to prevent brute-force attacks while still allowing legitimate users to request multiple resets if needed.

Test password reset request with email containing leading/trailing whitespace or embedded spaces. The system should either trim whitespace and process normally, or reject the request as invalid email format. Verify consistent behavior and that whitespace handling doesn't bypass validation or create duplicate token entries.

Test successful password reset with a valid, non-expired reset token and a new password meeting all security requirements (minimum 8 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special character). Verify that the password is hashed using bcrypt with minimum 12 salt rounds, the password_changed_at timestamp is updated, and all existing sessions for the contributor are invalidated. Confirm that the contributor can log in with the new password after reset.

Test password reset with a malformed or invalid token that doesn't match the expected cryptographic format. The system should reject the request without revealing specific token validity information. Verify that timing is consistent regardless of token validity to prevent timing-based attacks.

Test password reset with a valid token format that has exceeded the 30-minute validity window from generation. The system should reject the request with a generic error message that doesn't specifically reveal the token is expired (to prevent token enumeration). Verify that expired tokens are properly cleaned up from the database and cannot be reused.

Test password reset attempt with a reset token that has been previously used to successfully reset a password. Tokens are single-use and should become invalid after one successful reset. Verify that subsequent attempts with the same token are rejected without revealing that the token was already consumed. Confirm that the password reset actually persisted from the first successful use.

Test password reset with a new password that is fewer than 8 characters. The system should reject this with a validation error indicating the minimum length requirement. Verify that password validation occurs before any database modifications.

Test password reset with a new password that lacks uppercase letters (e.g., 'password1!'). The system should reject this with a validation error indicating the uppercase requirement. Verify that all character type requirements are validated.
Test password reset with a new password that lacks lowercase letters (e.g., 'PASSWORD1!'). The system should reject this with a validation error indicating the lowercase requirement.
Test password reset with a new password that lacks numeric digits (e.g., 'Password!'). The system should reject this with a validation error indicating the numeric digit requirement.
Test password reset with a new password that lacks special characters (e.g., 'Password123'). The system should reject this with a validation error indicating the special character requirement.

Test password reset with a new password that matches the contributor's previous password. The system should reject this to prevent reuse of recently compromised credentials. Verify that password history is checked before allowing the reset and that an appropriate error message is returned.
Test password reset with empty or null reset token field. The system should reject this as a required field validation error before any token validation is attempted.

Test that after a successful password reset, all existing sessions for the contributor are immediately invalidated. This forces re-authentication on all devices and sessions. Create a session/token before reset, perform the password reset, and verify that the old session token can no longer be used for authenticated requests. Confirm that a new login with the new password generates a new valid session.

Test that the password_changed_at timestamp is correctly updated to the current time upon successful password reset. This timestamp is critical for security auditing and session management. Verify that the timestamp reflects the exact time of the password change and is properly recorded in the database.

Test password reset with a new password containing unicode/international characters (e.g., émojis, Chinese characters, accented letters). Verify that the system properly handles and validates unicode characters, and that such passwords are correctly hashed and can be used for subsequent logins.

scenario.draft: Test password security requirements validation during registration. Attempt registration with passwords that fail security constraints: too short (less than 8 characters), missing uppercase letters, missing lowercase letters, missing numbers, missing special characters. Test that email address uniqueness constraint is enforced during registration. First, register a contributor with email 'alice@example.com'. Then attempt to register another contributor with the same email address. The second registration should fail with email already exists error, while the first account remains active and unchanged.

Test username format and uniqueness constraints. Test valid usernames: 'alice_123', 'Bob_Smith', 'user_1'. Test invalid usernames that violate constraints: too short ('ab'), too long (51+ characters), containing special characters ('alice@bob'), containing spaces ('alice smith'), containing hyphens ('alice-bob'). Verify format violations are rejected. Also test that duplicate usernames are rejected when attempting to register with an already-used username.

Test email format validation during registration. Attempt registration with invalid email formats: missing @ symbol, missing domain, invalid domain format, extra spaces, special characters not allowed in email format. Verify each invalid format is rejected. Then successfully register with valid email formats: standard format (user@domain.com), subdomain (user@mail.domain.com), numeric domains.

Test that session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are properly captured during registration. Register contributor with valid IP address, href URL pointing to registration page, and referrer URL indicating source page. Verify that these session context fields are recorded in the system for security monitoring and audit trails. Test that registration succeeds with null IP (server can extract), but fails if href or referrer are missing.

Test that JWT tokens are properly generated upon successful registration. After successful registration, verify that response includes access token (valid 30 minutes) and refresh token (valid 7 days) with proper expired_at and refreshable_until timestamps in ISO 8601 format. Validate token structure contains required fields and timestamps are in the future relative to registration time.

Test retrieving articles filtered by creation date range using createdDateFrom and createdDateTo parameters. Verify that only articles created within the specified date range are returned, with inclusive bounds on both start and end dates.

scenario.draft: Test pagination functionality when retrieving categories. Request multiple pages with different limit values and verify correct pagination behavior. Validate that pagination metadata (current, limit, records, pages) accurately reflects the data set. Test edge cases: requesting the last page, requesting a page beyond available data, and requesting with limit=0. Confirm that each page returns the correct subset of categories and pagination counters are accurate for proper UI navigation.

Test scenario where no categories exist in the system. If possible, verify the API returns an empty data array with correct pagination metadata (records=0, pages=0). Validate that the response structure remains consistent with pagination information even when no categories are available. This tests robustness when the category system is initially empty or all categories are inactive.

Test that inactive categories are properly excluded from the list. Verify the filtering mechanism by confirming only categories with is_active=true are returned. If the system has mixed active and inactive categories, validate that inactive ones do not appear in the response. This ensures users only see available categories for article submission and selection.

Test that each category in the list includes complete metadata needed for UI rendering. Verify each category object contains: id (UUID format), code (5-50 lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens), name (10-100 character human-readable title), display_order (non-negative integer), is_active (boolean), and article_count (non-negative integer). Validate data types and format constraints are satisfied for all fields.

Test that categories are returned in correct display_order sequence. Verify lower display_order values appear before higher values in the response. This confirms the UI will present categories in the intended sequence for consistent navigation and category menu ordering. Test with multiple categories having various display_order values to ensure proper sorting.

Test that the article_count field accurately reflects the number of published articles in each category. Verify that article_count is a non-negative integer and represents meaningful data for displaying category statistics (e.g., 'Economic Policy (47 articles)') in the user interface. Validate that this denormalized count matches the actual article count for each category.

Test that all required fields are present in the category detail response. Verify: id (UUID format), code (5-50 lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens), name (10-100 characters), display_order (non-negative integer), is_active (boolean), article_count (non-negative integer), created_at (ISO 8601 datetime), and updated_at (ISO 8601 datetime). Confirm no required fields are missing or null. This ensures API contract compliance.

Test that created_at and updated_at timestamps are properly formatted in ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z'). Verify timestamps are valid datetime values that can be parsed by standard ISO 8601 parsers. Confirm that updated_at is greater than or equal to created_at, indicating proper audit trail.

Test API behavior when requesting a category that does not exist. Provide a valid UUID format that corresponds to no category in the system. Verify the API returns an appropriate error response (404 Not Found expected). Validate error message is descriptive and helps clients understand the category was not found. This tests error handling for invalid resource requests.

Test API validation of malformed categoryId parameter. Provide invalid UUID formats (e.g., 'invalid-id', '12345', 'not-a-uuid') and verify the API properly rejects these with validation error. Confirm error response indicates parameter format requirement. This tests input validation and error handling for malformed identifiers.

Test API behavior when accessing a soft-deleted category (deleted_at is not null). Verify the API either returns 404 Not Found or returns restricted category data based on authorization level. If the category should not be accessible after soft deletion, confirm it is properly excluded from retrieval. This tests data integrity and soft-delete semantics.

Test that the category code field is properly validated as a unique machine-readable identifier. Verify the code follows the required format: 5-50 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens (e.g., 'economic-policy', 'political-governance'). Confirm that codes with invalid patterns (uppercase letters, special characters other than hyphens, incorrect length) are rejected. This ensures code integrity for API references and internal routing.

Test that category name field respects configured constraints. Verify names are between 10-100 characters and display as human-readable text suitable for UI display. Test edge cases: exactly 10 characters, exactly 100 characters, and names outside these bounds. Confirm that names are properly validated and formatted for user-facing display.

Test successful retrieval of all active content guidelines as a guest user. Verify that the endpoint returns a paginated list containing multiple guidelines with essential policy information including code, title, severity level, and active status. Validate pagination metadata shows correct page count, current page, limit, and total records. Confirm that guidelines are sorted by display_order for proper presentation in policy documentation. This tests the core functionality of the public guidelines listing API.

Test pagination behavior on the first page of guidelines list. Verify that pagination metadata returns current page = 0, and that the returned guidelines array contains up to the limit (20 items). Validate that the total records count and pages count are calculated correctly. Ensure first page fetches without issues and follows pagination conventions.

Test pagination functionality across multiple pages of guidelines list. Verify that when retrieving different pages via pagination parameters, the response correctly reflects the current page number and contains the appropriate subset of guidelines. Validate that the pagination metadata properly indicates pages available and total records, enabling clients to iterate through all guidelines efficiently.

Test behavior when no active guidelines exist in the system. Verify that the endpoint gracefully handles the scenario where there are no active guidelines to return by responding with an empty data array while maintaining proper pagination structure with records = 0 and pages = 0. Validate error handling does not crash and returns valid response structure.

Test that the endpoint returns only active guidelines (is_active = true). Verify that guidelines with is_active = false are excluded from the list, ensuring only currently enforced policies are presented to moderators and contributors. Validate that the filtering happens server-side and no inactive guidelines appear in results.
